semantic_slots.quantifiers: The space types and real δ are implicit, the measurable-space, probability and Markov assumptions are typeclass arguments, and the same K is fixed for both inputs. The universal measurable-input-event bound implies a universal measurable-output-event bound.

semantic_slots.conclusion: For every measurable t, the absolute difference of the real masses assigned by the two actual composed laws is at most δ. The prose follow-up asking for examples does not enlarge the Lean proposition.
semantic_slots.senses: For probabilities, .real is ordinary finite event mass. For measurable t, composition is integration of K(x,t) against the input law. The event-supremum probability-TV interpretation agrees with the decoder; neither the supremum nor a signed-measure norm is part of the signature.
semantic_slots.constants: Exactly the same real δ occurs on each side; factor one, no additive slack. The empty input event forces δ ≥ 0; δ need not be optimal or at most one. No change of TV normalization is implicit.
